text: A coracle, tied up and patient. {lead} takes the paddle and you take a seat. The water is easy and the other side has Willow Sprig.
Soft ground, a patient creature, and a lot of worms. {lead} brings up the lot, and under them: Truffle.
{lead} circles the flock like it has done this all its life. The gate is clear in a minute. Someone has hung Miniature Tin Bath on the post.
A gap in the wall, where the stones have gone for a walk. {lead} fits them back one by one, like a very slow jigsaw. Tucked in the wall behind: Fresnel Prism.
A molehill, freshly heaped. {lead} drums a gentle rhythm on the ground and the worms come up to see what the fuss is. Among the soil: a roll of notes.
A knot of sheep, all facing the wrong way. {lead} works them in a neat curve until the gate is clear. Left on the post for you: Double Gloucester.
Something glints in the water. {lead} wades in, makes a few calm passes and fishes it out: Lucky Sixpence.
The drystone has slumped. {lead} lifts the big stones in first and wedges the small ones after, which is exactly how it is done. Behind the stones: Lucky Sixpence.
A molehill, freshly heaped. {lead} drums a gentle rhythm on the ground and the worms come up to see what the fuss is. Among the soil: Colliery Check Tag.
Sheep at the gate, and no sheep will go first. {lead} comes round the back, low and quiet, and the flock files through. The farmer's thanks: a few coins.
The bog water is dark and cold. {lead} ploughs through it with its face down and surfaces holding a few coins.
{lead} lofts the bowl clear over the hedge and the bale makes a fine step. You scramble over after it, picking out the odd twig.
You go back over the bale, and {lead} lofts the bowl after you. A passing cyclist nods, as if this is normal.
A molehill, freshly heaped. {lead} drums a gentle rhythm on the ground and the worms come up to see what the fuss is. Among the soil: a roll of notes.
{lead} shoves the dead trunk over the gap, where it lands with a satisfying thump. You walk across, arms out like a tightrope act.
You cross back over the trunk, arms out. {lead} goes under the stream bank, which is its own business.
Soft ground, a patient creature, and a lot of worms. {lead} brings up the lot, and under them: Sheepdog Whistle.
